All three casings (`outputs`, `OUTPUTS`, `Outputs`) now yield the same `hits=11`, matching `grep -ic`, confirming case-insensitive ASCII matching works correctly while `check.sh` passes.

**Summary:** In `bench.py`'s `find` mode, both the `data.count` and per-line loop paths now fold ASCII letters via `bytes.lower()` (which only remaps `A`–`Z`, leaving all other bytes byte-exact) before matching, making the substring scan case-insensitive for ASCII letters while preserving exact matching for everything else and the once-per-line counting in `find.loop`. Verified with `sh check.sh` and manual case-variant checks against `fixtures/store.txt`.
bash:
python3 -c "
b = bytes(range(256))
print(b.lower() == bytes((c+32 if 65<=c<=90 else c) for c in range(256)))
"
sh check.sh

grep -ic "outputs" fixtures/store.txt
python3 bench.py find fixtures/store.txt outputs | head -1
python3 bench.py find fixtures/store.txt OUTPUTS | head -1
python3 bench.py find fixtures/store.txt Outputs | head -1
